title: mypy
description: Check Python types to find incompatible arguments, return values, and operations without running the program.
markdown: # mypy ## Where it fits Use mypy to check whether code uses the types described by annotations and stubs consistently. It complements [Ruff](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/ruff/) for linting and [Bandit](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/bandit/) for selected Python security patterns. A clean lint run is not a type-checking result. Gradual typing lets a project adopt annotations in stages. By default, bodies of functions without annotations receive limited checking. `Any` and ignored imports can also let type mistakes pass unnoticed. ## First try **Illustrative example, not run here.** Follow the [mypy installation instructions](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/getting_started.html) in your selected Python environment, then save this as `sample.py`: ```python def next_count(count: int) -> int: return count + 1 next_count("three") ``` Check it without running the program: ```sh python -m mypy sample.py ``` Representative diagnostic, not captured output (formatting varies by version): ```text sample.py:4: error: Argument 1 to "next_count" has incompatible type "str"; expected "int" [arg-type] ``` `sample.py:4` locates the call. `arg-type` identifies an incompatible argument type: text was passed to an integer parameter. Replace the argument with `3` and check again. This example exercises one mismatch, not the entire type system. See the [argument-type diagnostic reference](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/error_code_list.html#check-argument-types-arg-type) for details. Use the [shared Ruff and mypy recipe](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/guides/python-checks/) for a pinned environment, faulty/corrected files, and separate reports. ## Configure a useful check Supply the project's imports and any required third-party stubs. Start with a small annotated area, inspect errors, and tighten the configuration deliberately. `--check-untyped-defs` can inspect unannotated bodies, while `--strict` enables a broader set of checks. Record the mypy version, configuration, target Python version, and suppressions. Static types do not validate arbitrary input data at runtime or replace application tests. [Compare mypy, Ruff, and Bandit](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/compare/?tools=tools%2Fmypy%2Ctools%2Fruff%2Ctools%2Fbandit) to see their different roles. ## Compare Python type checkers [Pyright](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/pyright/) is another Python type checker. Both use annotations and stubs, but configuration, inference, diagnostics, and plugin support differ. For a useful trial, check the same revision with matching Python version, platform, imports, and intended strictness. Investigate disagreements instead of comparing diagnostic counts. Keep [mypy import and stub settings](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html) and [Pyright settings](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) with the reports. [Compare mypy and Pyright](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/compare/?tools=tools%2Fmypy%2Ctools%2Fpyright). Ruff remains complementary for lint rules; running two type checkers is a deliberate evaluation choice, not a requirement of the Python recipe. - **Summary:** Check Python types to find incompatible arguments, return values, and operations without running the program. - **Use it for:** Check whether Python annotations, calls, and return values agree in a configured project. - **What you need:** Provide Python files, type annotations, configuration, and relevant dependencies or stubs. No application execution or test harness is required. - **What you get:** Diagnostics name the file, line, type mismatch, and error code, such as arg-type for an incompatible argument. - **Checks and limits:** Any, missing stubs, untyped code, and suppressions can hide mistakes. A clean check does not validate runtime input or behavior. - **Finding scope:** Checks type consistency in the analyzed code. Any, missing stubs, ignored errors, and untyped functions can reduce coverage; it does not prove runtime correctness. ## Compatibility and scope - **Also known as:** mypy type checker - **Analysis mode:** Static - **What it examines:** Source code - **Context:** Python applications, Libraries, Type stubs - **Techniques:** Type checking - **Finding categories:** Type errors - **Where it runs:** A local or CI Python environment. The current getting-started guide requires Python 3.10 or later to run mypy. - **Languages / ecosystem:** Python - **Language support:** Python source and type stubs. Match the target Python version and platform settings to the project; these can differ from the interpreter running mypy. - **Edition and scope:** The mypy command-line type checker and its documented gradual-typing workflow. This entry does not cover general security scanning or runtime type enforcement. ## Cost and editions - **Cost:** Free - **Cost conditions:** Free open-source type checker. Local use does not require a hosted service or paid analyzer edition. - **License category:** Open source - **License:** MIT, with additional notices for bundled components Cost information checked 2026-09-26. Runtimes, hosting, and compute may cost extra. Free trials are not counted as free editions. ## Sources and evidence [Official website](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) - [Type checking and gradual typing](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) - [Installation, annotations, and strictness](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/getting_started.html) - [Imports, stubs, and analysis scope](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/running_mypy.html) - [Missing errors and other limitations](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/common_issues.html) - [License and bundled notices](https://github.com/python/mypy/blob/master/LICENSE) - [Pyright configuration for comparable checks](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/main/docs/configuration.md) Source: [ToolWiki page](https://zwadhams.github.io/ToolWiki/tools/mypy/).
